intro: A gated feed-forward block uses one projection to form values and another to control their contribution. SwiGLU applies a smooth SiLU gate before an output projection.
task: Trace the value and gate branches separately, multiply them element by element, then project the gated features back to the output space.
requirements: x has nonempty shape (..., input_features). w_value and w_gate both have shape (input_features, hidden_features), and w_out has shape (hidden_features, output_features); every dimension is positive.
Let h=x@w_value and g=x@w_gate. Return (h*(g*sigmoid(g)))@w_out as a NumPy array with the leading shape of x and output_features last.
Use a stable sigmoid for large positive and negative g. There are no bias parameters or gradient updates in this contract.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Keep the branches distinct
hints.body: Applying the sigmoid to h instead of g changes the model even when the matrix shapes still fit.

hints.title: Avoid exp of a large positive number
hints.body: For negative g, use exp(g)/(1+exp(g)); for nonnegative g, use 1/(1+exp(-g)).

explanation: The gate can be negative because SiLU(g)=g*sigmoid(g). Replacing it with sigmoid alone removes its amplitude and sign behavior.
A zero gate projection makes every output zero, while a nonzero value projection alone cannot restore the output. This exposes the multiplicative interaction.
Ported the upstream SwiGLU forward equation to NumPy and added stable sigmoid evaluation, explicit matrix conventions and immutable inputs.
